brief: An 8-second before/after split screen: a vertical divider draws down the middle; the left half is titled 'Before' and shows a messy scatter of 12 gray dots; the right half is titled 'After' and shows the same 12 dots animating from a scatter into a neat 3 by 4 grid in blue.
checks: Does a vertical line appear at the top‑center of the frame and extend downward to the bottom‑center, finishing its draw before the video ends?
Is the left half of the frame labeled with the text “Before” in a legible, high‑contrast style?
Is the right half of the frame labeled with the text “After” in a legible, high‑contrast style?
In the left half, are there exactly 12 dots, all colored gray, arranged in a scattered, non‑grid pattern?
At the start of the right‑half animation, are there exactly 12 dots that match the initial positions of the left‑half scatter?
Do the 12 dots in the right half animate from their scattered start positions to form a precise 3‑by‑4 grid (3 columns, 4 rows) by the end of the video?
Are the dots in the right half colored blue (or a shade of blue) throughout their animation while the left‑half dots remain gray?
Does the vertical divider complete its full height before the dot animation begins, establishing a clear before/after separation?
At no point do any dot, text, or the divider touch or cross the outer frame edges?
Are the divider, titles, and dot clusters aligned to a clear vertical layout with even spacing between the left and right halves and consistent margins?
Do all movements (the divider drawing and the dot transitions) use easing (slow‑in/slow‑out) rather than moving at a constant speed?
Is there at least some visual change occurring in every one‑second interval of the video (no dead‑air seconds), and does nothing appear before the first 0.5 second?
Does the final frame hold still (no further animation) for at least 0.5 second before the video ends?
Are the gray and blue colors harmonious, and are there no visible glitches, flicker, overlapping text, or rendering artifacts?
